answer: Endorsements are edges; each close partitions the attestation graph into islands. Pools pay only islands above node cap K that hold an edge to a pre-epoch node. A fresh sybil farm is a small island: internal edges earn nothing, since it fails K and has no bridge. Passing means bribing K distinct pre-epoch identities, making the farm costlier than the pool it can extract. A lone lotus mimics a hundred in an open pond; only a cluster rooted in the old marsh claims the nectar, so each island's share is capped by pre-epoch bridge edges.
